- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent 7-day average to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1), model often fails to anticipate sharp downside; add 1–2% buffer below recent low to account for volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate downward moves in bearish sentiment; apply a 1–3% upward adjustment if sentiment < 0.4 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is flat, model often overpredicts volatility; reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to reflect lack of momentum.
